gradingSemantic: CURRENT COLLEGE FOOTBALL ABILITY AT WIDE RECEIVER RIGHT NOW; 2026 is the leading evidence, 2025 substantially stabilizes, older evidence is secondary. Evaluate separation/release, route running, hands, catch-point ability, YAC/creation, vertical threat, ball security and overall receiving usefulness. No NFL projection, recruiting ranking, draft stock, fame/school prestige, fantasy value, or future-upside bonus.
currentSeasonWeighting: Middle-ground CFB standard locked by Cody: approximately 55-60% current 2026 performance/role, 30-35% 2025 demonstrated level, remainder older/context; conceptual guidance, not a literal formula.

resolvedPressurePoints: Carlos Hernandez moves above the original anchor board's 94 tier after the full-population audit because 516 yards through four games plus a real 2025 sample make the current level elite.
Collin Dixon holds 94 despite EA 87 because 430 yards and seven TD through four games are not a one-game spike.
Cam Coleman remains the approved 89 reputation checkpoint; traits and prior ability are real, but 2026 production does not justify EA's elite rating.
Koby Young, DJ Epps, Chris Durr, Amare Thomas and Ed Small were all reduced from the initial full-board pass where current counting stats were being overweighted.
The bottom remains deliberately separated; a curated WR slot does not imply an 80 floor.

rangeSeparationAudit.note: Secondary receivers, thin-sample players and weak Wheel options are allowed into the 70s. No grade was raised merely because the player survived curation.

eaDiscrepancyAudit.source: EA SPORTS College Football 27 current Week 4 WR ratings where exact current entries could be resolved
eaDiscrepancyAudit.rule: Absolute HQ-vs-EA difference of 7+ requires mandatory review; 10+ requires explicit major-red-flag explanation. EA is an error detector, never a formula or required midpoint.

mandatoryReviews.explanation: Keep HQ 92. The current four-game breakout and physical receiving profile are materially ahead of EA 84; the grade is high-end, not ceiling-level, because the established sample is less complete.
Keep HQ 94. He has 430 yards and seven TD through four games, including a credible 63-yard showing at Ohio State. EA has moved him up but still trails the current football evidence.
Keep HQ 88. Four-game production (24 catches, 371 yards) is a real sophomore breakout; 88 recognizes that without pretending his limited prior sample makes him elite.
Keep HQ 85. EA 78 is too low after 279 yards/3 TD through four games plus a 512-yard 2025 season, but the audit already reduced HQ from 91 to 85 to avoid overreacting to explosive-play production.
Keep HQ 95. His 2026 production is elite (30 catches, 516 yards, 3 TD through four games) and is supported by a 611-yard 2025 season. EA 87 is clearly lagging the current level.

runtimeBoundary: No production/runtime behavior is changed by this artifact. It is calibration authority only for later server-owned Wheel grading integration.
futureVersioning: Any future WR grade change must record previous grade, new grade, effective date, concise football reason, and nearby anchor/peer sanity check. Normal maintenance is a targeted exception scan, not a wholesale regrade.
